natural_body: SMB 40% discounts lifted acquisition and near-term revenue but cut retention 12%.

first.rationale: We face simultaneous drops in activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ). Memory 91 demonstrates that activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and first meaningful action. This directly addresses the activation decline we're seeing. Memory 86 shows onboarding shortening lifted adoption, and memory 31 confirmed signup simplification drove durable SMB activation gains. Rather than chase competitor pricing (memory 73 showed 40% discounts hurt retention by 12%, creating long-term damage to our primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue), we should double down on what we control: product-driven activation. Activation messaging is lower-risk than promotional pricing, doesn't cannibalize existing customers like referrals might in a declining market, and directly targets the root metric decline. Verifying memories 31 and 91 will confirm the effect sizes and cohort characteristics to calibrate message framing and targeting. This preserves our optionality for pricing or referral approaches if activation messaging underperforms, and avoids the retention risk that aggressive SMB discounting carries.
